analysis.note: Relative pronoun; object of vyathayanti, resumed by saḥ.

Parasmaipada present, 3rd plural; recorded as the aya-present/transitive verbal base vyathay after verifier rejection of the previous √vyath analysis. Semantically, Śaṅkara glosses it with cālayanti, “shake/disturb.”
Subject of vyathayanti; Śaṅkara identifies the referents as the previously stated śītoṣṇa and the like.
Accusative object, qualified by sama-duḥkha-sukham and dhīram.

verification.detail: compound stem puruṣarṣabha as Pum/Sambodhana/Eka: pass; relation tatpurusa: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Bahuvrīhi adjective agreeing with puruṣam/dhīram; not a neuter object “equal pain-and-pleasure.” The verifier reported a tool_error for this compound inflection and does not support validating bahuvrīhi relation; retained on the explicit commentary vigraha same duḥkha-sukhe yasya.

verification.detail: compound stem sama-duḥkha-sukha as Pum/Dvitiya/Eka: pass; relation bahuvrihi: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Correlative pronoun resuming yam; external sandhi saḥ + amṛtatvāya > so ’mṛtatvāya.
Abstract noun in -tva; Śaṅkara glosses it as amṛta-bhāva and mokṣa.
Ātmanepada; with dative amṛtatvāya, “is capable/fit,” per Śaṅkara’s samartho bhavati.

justifications.decision: The compound qualifies the accusative puruṣam/dhīram; it is not a neuter object meaning “equal pain-and-pleasure” as a thing.
options_considered: karmadhāraya/dvandva-like description of equal pain-and-pleasure as a neuter entity
justifications.chosen: sama-duḥkha-sukhaṃ is a bahuvrīhi: “one for whom pain and pleasure are the same,” specifically free from elation and dejection at their occurrence.

evidence.quote: same duḥkha-sukhe yasya taṃ sama-duḥkha-sukhaṃ sukha-duḥkha-prāptau harṣa-viṣāda-rahitaṃ
evidence.translation: “sama-duḥkha-sukha” means him for whom pain and pleasure are the same, free from joy and despondency when pleasure and pain are obtained.

justifications.decision: Śaṅkara explicitly glosses dhīra as dhīmān, so the translation foregrounds wisdom/intelligence rather than courage alone.
options_considered: emotionally steady without reference to knowledge
justifications.chosen: dhīraṃ is rendered “wise,” with steadiness implied by understanding, not merely “brave.”

justifications.decision: The subject is not “these people” or an unspecified set; Śaṅkara identifies it as yathoktāḥ śītoṣṇādayaḥ and glosses vyathayanti by cālayanti.
options_considered: these = cold/heat and other dualities from the prior verse
justifications.chosen: ete refers to the previously mentioned cold-and-heat and the like; vyathayanti means “disturb/shake.”

evidence.quote: na vyathayanti na cālayanti nityātma-darśanāt ete yathoktāḥ śītoṣṇādayaḥ
evidence.translation: They do not disturb, do not shake, because of the vision of the eternal self; these are the aforementioned cold-and-heat and so on.

justifications.decision: kalpate is not taken as “imagines” or simply “becomes”; Śaṅkara glosses it as samartho bhavati. amṛtatva is not mere long life or divine nectar but mokṣa.
justifications.chosen: amṛtatvāya kalpate means “is fit/capable for immortality,” where immortality is liberation (mokṣa).

evidence.quote: amṛtatvāya amṛta-bhāvāya mokṣāyety arthaḥ kalpate samartho bhavati
evidence.translation: “For immortality” means for the state of being immortal, that is, for liberation; “kalpate” means becomes capable/fit.

justifications.decision: The commentary is silent on this address; grammar and dictionary decide it. MW s.v. ṛṣabha, 226,3 gives “a bull” and “the best or most excellent of any kind or race,” explicitly comparing forms such as puruṣarṣabha.
options_considered: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa: puruṣāṇām ṛṣabhaḥ, best among men
karmadhāraya: a man who is a literal bull
justifications.chosen: puruṣarṣabha is a vocative tatpuruṣa, “O bull/best among men.”

translation:
For the wise person, O best among men,
whom these [cold-and-heat and the like] do not shake,
equal in pain and pleasure—
he is fit for immortality (amṛtatva), that is, liberation.
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation might leave sama-duḥkha-sukha as a vague “having equal pain and pleasure”; Śaṅkara makes it an inner freedom from joy and despondency when pleasure and pain arise.
It might render amṛtatva as literal immortality only; Śaṅkara identifies it as mokṣa, liberation.
It might take dhīra primarily as “brave” or “stoic”; Śaṅkara glosses it as dhīmān, wise.
It might leave ete unspecified or read it as people/enemies; Śaṅkara says it is the previously mentioned cold-and-heat and the like.
It might translate kalpate as “becomes” or “is made”; Śaṅkara’s samartho bhavati supports “is fit/capable.”
analyzer_disagreements: sama-duḥkha-sukham: ByT5 presents the members separately with final sukham; the analysis here records the whole inflected compound stem sama-duḥkha-sukha, masculine accusative singular, because it qualifies puruṣam/dhīram and Śaṅkara supplies the bahuvrīhi vigraha same duḥkha-sukhe yasya.
amṛtatvāya: ByT5 segments amṛta + tvāya; the apparatus treats the form as the single derived abstract noun amṛtatva, neuter dative singular, supported by Śaṅkara’s amṛta-bhāvāya mokṣāya.
puruṣarṣabha: ByT5’s puruṣa + ṛṣabha segmentation is retained as compound membership, but the inflected word is recorded under the internally sandhied compound stem puruṣarṣabha.
mula: yaṃ hi na vyathayanty ete puruṣaṃ puruṣarṣabha | sama-duḥkha-sukhaṃ dhīraṃ so 'mṛtatvāya kalpate
commentary_lines: yaṃ hi puruṣaṃ same duḥkha-sukhe yasya taṃ sama-duḥkha-sukhaṃ sukha-duḥkha-prāptau harṣa-viṣāda-rahitaṃ dhīraṃ dhīmantaṃ na vyathayanti na cālayanti nityātma-darśanāt ete yathoktāḥ śītoṣṇādayaḥ, sa nityātma-svarūpa-darśa-niṣṭho dvandva-sahiṣṇuḥ amṛtatvāya amṛta-bhāvāya mokṣāyety arthaḥ kalpate samartho bhavati ||bhgs_2.15||
